❯ Do these four things in order and nothing else. One: write me two full sentences of prose about why integration
  tests are worth their cost. Two: run the shell command echo kampr-probe-prose with the Bash tool. Three: write me
  one more full sentence of prose saying what that command printed. Four: use the AskUserQuestion tool to ask me which
  suite to run, with the options unit and integration. Do not write any files.

● Integration tests are worth their cost because they exercise the seams between components — the wiring, the
  serialization, the process boundaries — where the defects that actually reach users tend to live, and no amount of
  unit coverage on either side of a seam proves the seam itself holds. They also stay honest as the implementation
  churns underneath them: a unit test pinned to an internal function has to be rewritten every time that function
  moves, while an integration test that drives the real thing end to end keeps asserting the behaviour anyone cares
  about.
